title: Pyramid of Meidum, Beni Suef
summary: The Meidum pyramid in Egypt's Beni Suef region grew from a seven-step pyramid to an eight-step one and was finally given smooth sides as a true pyramid about 92 to 95 m high on a 144 m base. It is linked with King Sneferu. Its outer layers are gone, leaving a three-step core in a mound of rubble.

uncertainty.note: Start is the first year of Sneferu's reign as the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities dates it (c. 2613-2589 BC, astronomical -2612). The Penn Museum says ca. 2600 BCE, and earlier attribution to Huni (c. 2637-2613 BC) is called no longer the consensus. End is the present.

reviewer_note: Shape pyramid, showing the final E3 phase at the lower 92 m bound of the sourced 92-95 m. The ruin today is far lower. The 'ruined' phase start is the year after Sneferu's reign ends and is not a sourced collapse date. No building material is stated on the opened pages. The Penn page says only 'over 300 feet' for height, not used.
